takeaway: Class I haemorrhagic shock is 0–15 per cent blood loss, with only a fast heart rate and everything else normal.

question.text: A 35-year-old woman with endometriosis bleeds heavily every month. Her heart rate is 105 beats/min; all other parameters are normal. Which degree of haemorrhagic shock?
question.say: A thirty-five-year-old woman with endometriosis bleeds heavily every month. Her heart rate is one hundred and five beats per minute, and everything else is normal. Which degree of haemorrhagic shock is this?

lines.text: Here is the calendar: endometriosis, and heavy bleeding every month.
lines.say: Here is the calendar. This woman has endometriosis, and she bleeds heavily every month.

lines.text: Yet she sips her tea calmly: everything else is normal.
lines.say: (laugh) Yet look at her, calmly sipping tea, because everything else is normal.

lines.text: The only change is a fast heart: HR 105.
lines.say: The only abnormal thing is a fast heart, one hundred and five beats per minute. That is tachycardia.

lines.text: The jug shows the loss: 0–15 per cent of the volume.
lines.say: The jug shows the loss: zero to fifteen per cent of the circulating volume. That is class one shock.

lines.text: In Class I there is only tachycardia.
lines.say: In class one shock there is only tachycardia, nothing else.

lines.text: Remember: a fast pulse with everything else normal is Class I.
lines.say: Remember: a fast pulse with everything else normal is class one shock.
